I am an old man now, eighty-four years, and this small maize plot is what feeds my household. My strength is not what it was, so my children and grandchildren help me on the land. If I receive the coupon from the government this year, I will buy the NPK and urea for my maize — without that coupon the price at the market is too much for me. I keep some goats and chickens, so I carry their manure to the field before the rains, and I plant pigeon pea between my maize rows as my father taught me, so the soil stays alive. I do not have money for pesticides, and there is no stream close enough to irrigate — I wait for the rains like everyone here in Mangochi.
